newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end strong as yen stabilises.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end strong as yen stabilises.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished on a high note on Tuesday as participants took heart in the yen's relatively stable tone against the dollar.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 275 points higher at 20,585 after touching a low of 20,170. September added 280 points to 20,630.
Dealers said the market came under pressure in early trade when the dollar fell sharply from around the 113.00 yen level. It was quoted at 112.99/113.04 yen at 0710 GMT in Tokyo.
"After the dollar/yen recovered, the market stayed in a narrow range. It was between 20,450 and 20,605 all afternoon," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said there was active switching over of positions to the September contract and added that the market was likely to remain in a 20,200-20,600 range until June's expiry on Thursday.

On Taiwan futures, the June MSCI contract ended higher at 356.9 following gains in the Taipei stock market where big-capital shares eligible for inclusion in the island's debut warrants drew buying interest.
